<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **56** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/getting-started/examples.mdx`  _(via task.object.ts (literal, a string literal in runSelfTest))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 743308b90c3a5877db980607c9cffd69ba6e5cd4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `159997536755dda74042d81f67333ed4a306cf6d` — the merge of head `c169dc85d571ae167e6dd63d5774a017cb07c987` into base `743308b90c3a5877db980607c9cffd69ba6e5cd4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 159997536755dda74042d81f67333ed4a306cf6d && git checkout 159997536755dda74042d81f67333ed4a306cf6d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 743308b90c3a5877db980607c9cffd69ba6e5cd4 c169dc85d571ae167e6dd63d5774a017cb07c987 && git checkout -B drift-repro 743308b90c3a5877db980607c9cffd69ba6e5cd4 && git merge --no-ff c169dc85d571ae167e6dd63d5774a017cb07c987

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 743308b90c3a5877db980607c9cffd69ba6e5cd4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 743308b90c3a5877db980607c9cffd69ba6e5cd4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 review · ACCEPT (nits only)** · Head-sha: `8d82dcb937777118cf574ab638b7d62e44fd9c57` · card #34789 (Part of) · read 2026-11-17T23:22Z

This is a full review: there is no earlier L1 record. I read the whole diff from merge-base `db1a05cd` (31 files, +941 / -85), plus the card, the body and dev report 6963882763.

**Surface.** Every path falls inside the card's file surface (`skills/*/evals/**`, `packages/qa/**`) except the changeset. Clause-② is `no` and Metadata-protocol is `none`. Both fit the diff: `src/skill-evals/` is in no tsup entry, export or bin, and the dist measurement is in the body. A `patch` for `@objectstack/scenarios` (README) and `@objectstack/skills` (evals ship as inert fixtures) is the right level.

**Runner.**
- **Reader** (`cases.ts`). `should_trigger` replaces `assertions`, and the two together are refused. A non-boolean kind is refused, and so is a bundle whose trigger cases are all one kind (the check runs per bundle, after the missing-file refusals). `hashCase` adds the extra object only when a case has a trigger kind or a non-empty `files`, so `JSON.stringify([prompt, mc, mnc])` is byte-identical for every unchanged behaviour case and `--regrade` stays valid. The 41 edited cases are set apart, not regraded.
- **Judge** (`run.ts`). A trigger case on the no-skill arm is `invalid`. On the with-skill arm, the existing init-line check still runs first. "Loaded" means a `Skill` launch of the bundle, or a `Read` whose path has `.claude/skills/BUNDLE/` in it. The `${bundle}/` prefix keeps a same-prefix bundle out, and a test pins that. A loaded turn is judged however it ended. An unloaded turn that did not end in `success` is `error`. Negatives accept a turn that is cut short only when it loaded the bundle, which can only fail them. That asymmetry is stated and pinned.
- **Plan and summary.** `armsOf` gives a trigger case one arm. Trigger records are tallied in `byTrigger` and `continue` before the behaviour tally, so they never enter a behaviour rate. `regradeRound` keeps trigger keys planned. `placeCaseFiles` copies into both arms after `prepareArmWorkdir`.
- **Tests.** 10 new tests cover each rule above, plus 8 self-test rows (floor 29). The body records an ablation of the read evidence, with 4 tests going red. I did not re-run it.

**Assertion edits: each one judged for over-reach.** All 11 are kept.
- `flows-triggers-approvals#13`: `.custom`. The skill spells the pair this way. `overrides:`, `basedOn` and `/toggle` still carry the case.
- `bundles-locales-coverage#10`: the narrowed forbid still catches the nested shape authored on one line. See N2.
- `hooks-security-seeds-datasources#14`: `'138****`. The prompt and `references/seeds.md` both carry the masked form, so the narrowing is right.
- `objects-fields-relationships#10`: the narrowed forbid tokens. Right, since the expected answer declines `required` by name. See N2.
- `objects-fields-relationships#12`: `filter:` is loose. The prompt names no field or value, though, and the two forbidden label forms carry the case.
- `objects-fields-relationships#14`: `value: '` is loose. The value is the author's choice, and the forbidden `value: '合作中'` carries the case.
- `views-apps-actions-pages#16`: right. The URL template stays exact, and only the formatting and the free param name are released.
- `skills-tools-knowledge#5` and `#6`: right. #6 still requires `signed-in session` and `refused`.
- `objectui/testing#2`: right.
- `protocol-major-upgrade#3`: right on the facts. The skill says "never ran" and "unexecuted", and the prompt carries the old forbid verbatim. See N2.

The 30 context sentences add context only. None of them hints at an answer. The two that gained facts (`endpoints-auth-routes#2` and `#6`) give what case #1 had held or what the prompt referred to, and none of their assertion tokens appears in that added text.

**Trigger cases.** There are 42: 7 per bundle, 5 positive and 2 negative, so every bundle has both kinds. Each bundle's negatives are a neighbouring skill's task and a near miss outside ObjectStack. The body states the limit of one bundle with no competitor present.

**Gates at this head (latest attempt per check, read 2026-11-17T23:22Z):** none failed, 25 success, 10 skipped, and 12 still running (Test Core, Test UI, Type Check, Lint). The derived families are 75 of 76 run locally, with `dual-build-cjs-loads` as a prerequisite that CI runs.

### Nits (each can become a card; none blocks)

- **N1: Grep is not load evidence.** The arms give `Read,Glob,Grep,Skill`. A `Grep` in content mode with its `path` under `.claude/skills/BUNDLE/` reaches the skill's text, but it is not counted. So a positive turn that greps the bundle and answers is a missed load. Before and after use the same rule, so #34769's comparison holds. Still, a third evidence kind shown apart (a Grep `path` under the bundle) would make the split honest.
- **N2: the narrowed forbid tokens bind one-line formatting.** That was the PR's own reason for loosening #16. A wrong shape written across lines escapes `verdict: { summary: '` and `transform: { type: 'javascript'`. So does `required: true` as the last key followed by a newline. The grader is a literal match and sits outside this card's surface. The card would be a whitespace-normalised match in `grade.ts`, or multi-line variants of these three tokens.
- **N3: `files` can plant into the arm's config.** `caseFileProblem` accepts `evals/files/.claude/…` and `evals/files/.mcp.json`, and `placeCaseFiles` would copy them into both arms' projects. A planted catalog skill would surface as `invalid` through the init line. Settings or a planted non-catalog skill would not. No case uses `files` today. Refusing a first segment of `.claude`, or a `.mcp.json`, would close it.

**Owed, for the seat:** the Tier H approval (governed per check-governed-merges: `skills/**`). The contract review face is the runner's grading contract (the trigger verdict and what counts as loaded). The card stays open for the eval seat's model round. This comment readies, queues and arms nothing.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8d82dcb937777118cf574ab638b7d62e44fd9c57`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json, skills/objectstack-api/evals/endpoints-auth-routes.json, skills/objectstack-automation/evals/flows-triggers-approvals.json, skills/objectstack-automation/evals/triggers.json, skills/objectstack-data/evals/README.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json, skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json, skills/objectstack-data/evals/triggers.json, skills/objectstack-formula/evals/triggers.json, skills/objectstack-i18n/evals/bundles-locales-coverage.json, skills/objectstack-i18n/evals/triggers.json, skills/objectstack-platform/evals/config-plugins-ops.json, skills/objectstack-query/evals/triggers.json, skills/objectstack-ui/evals/README.md, skills/objectstack-ui/evals/record-page.json, skills/objectstack-ui/evals/triggers.json, skills/objectstack-ui/evals/views-apps-actions-pages.json, skills/objectstack-upgrade/evals/protocol-major-upgrade.json, skills/objectui/evals/data-integration.json, skills/objectui/evals/page-builder.json, skills/objectui/evals/project-setup.json, skills/objectui/evals/testing.json + packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/run.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/cases.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/arms.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/summary.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/cli.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/self-test.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/README.md
Security-touching: yes

Read for this record: card #34789 (body and all five comments, through dev report 6963882763), PR #35022 (body, file list, net diff from merge-base `db1a05cd`, 31 files, +941 / -85) and the check-runs on the head. The rest of the diff (the test file, the changeset text) is the lane seat's ACCEPT.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-11-17T23:32Z: 36 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 3 still running (`Test Core (1/10)`, `Test Core (2/10)`, `Test UI (1/16)`). The lint, type-check, changeset, PR-size, PR-body and Governed Surface Queue Guard runs are all success. The three running shards have no verdict yet; the seat reads them before it adopts this record.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Eval-file accept-set, widened: right.** `parseEvalFile` now accepts an entry with a boolean `should_trigger` and no `assertions`. It refuses a non-boolean kind, a trigger case that also carries `assertions`, a `files` value that is not a list of strings, and a `files` entry that is not a path under `evals/files/`. `loadSkillEvalCatalog` refuses a `files` path the bundle lacks and a bundle whose trigger cases are all one kind. A behaviour case is read exactly as before (same refusals, same order of checks). The one gap in this accept-set is S1 below.
- **Case hash: right.** `hashCase` appends the extra object only when a case has a trigger kind or a non-empty `files`, so the hashed string for an unchanged behaviour case is byte-identical to main's and old rounds still regrade. The 41 edited cases hash differently and are set apart, which is the existing rule.
- **Round plan: right.** `armsOf` gives a trigger case the with-skill arm only; `verdictOf` reads a trigger case on the no-skill arm as `invalid`. 217 behaviour cases on two arms plus 42 trigger cases on one is 476 turns, as the body states.
- **Record and summary shape, widened: right.** Every record gains `skillFilesRead`; a trigger record gains `trigger`. `RoundSummary` gains a required `triggers` block; `regradeRound` reads it as optional, so a round recorded on main still regrades. Trigger records `continue` before the behaviour tally and never enter a behaviour rate.
- **Published surface: none beyond text.** `src/skill-evals/` is in no export, bin or tsup entry of `@objectstack/scenarios` (the body's dist measurement; the type-check and build check-runs are green). `@objectstack/skills` gains six `evals/triggers.json` files, inert in a consumer install.
- **Other readers of `skills/*/evals/*.json`.** `ui/scripts/check-skill-eval-tokens.mjs` reads `item.assertions ?? {}`, so an entry with no `assertions` reads as empty lists there; `Lint UI` is success on this head.
- **Security-touching is `yes`, and meant narrowly.** Changed hunks sit on cases whose subject is authentication and credentials: `objectstack-api/endpoints-auth-routes#2` (an endpoint made callable without login; the prompt is rewritten), `objectstack-ai/skills-tools-knowledge#6` (an API token refused on the approve door; one required token dropped), and `objectstack-data/objects-fields-relationships#1` (a prompt with an API key and a password field). No hunk changes which security behaviour a case passes or fails: #2's assertions are untouched, and #6 keeps `signed-in session`, `refused` and the forbidden `pendingActions.approve(`. The PR is governed on other grounds as well (paths outside `skills/**`, six catalog files added), so the low-risk arm does not apply either way.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no. The changeset is `patch` for `@objectstack/scenarios` (README text only reaches the package) and `patch` for `@objectstack/skills` (new and edited eval fixtures). That matches what the diff publishes: no exported symbol, no CLI flag, no schema. The changeset and the PR body both carry `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. `Check Changeset` is success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, narrowed local runs while the verify lock was held: answered by the head's check-runs, which are the gate verdicts here.
- Deviation, `Clause-②: no` carried with no parenthetical arm: right for a measured `no`.
- Deviation, PR assignee set by `pr_create`: no contract effect.
- `unmet`, the model round was not run: the PR says `Part of #34789` and the card stays open for the eval seat. Right; nothing in this diff claims a measured result.
- Out-of-scope finding, `objectstack-api/endpoints-auth-routes#6` requires `sourceField` / `targetField`, taught only by the spec source: confirmed (`packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts`). Left on the card for the round to show; not this PR's to fix.
- Out-of-scope finding, `objectstack-automation/flows-triggers-approvals#16` requires `notices.`, taught by the data bundle: same answer.
- SQL push-down: no query, id materialisation or join in this diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**The trigger verdict (`run.ts`).** The code agrees with its jsdoc and with the README, sentence by sentence.

- Loaded means a `Skill` tool call whose `skill` is the bundle, or a `Read` whose `file_path` holds `.claude/skills/BUNDLE/` followed by a file. The `BUNDLE/` prefix keeps a same-prefix bundle and a read of the bare directory out.
- The existing arm check runs first: a with-skill turn whose init line does not list the bundle is `invalid` before any trigger reading. All six metadata bundles are listed bundles.
- A turn that loaded the bundle is judged however it ended. A turn that did not is judged only on `success`, and is `error` otherwise. That is symmetric in what it excludes: a cut-short unloaded turn leaves the denominator for positive and negative cases alike. It cannot inflate either side, since a cut-short turn can only move a positive toward pass or a negative toward fail when the load is in the stream.
- The trigger case runs on one arm, so there is no between-arm comparison to bias. The comparison the card wants is between two rounds (before and after #34769) under the same rule.
- `summariseRound` counts the Skill-tool and read-only splits over judged turns only, per case.

**The reader and the catalog (`cases.ts`).** Refusals are located and precede any grading; the CLI throws on any refusal. The one-kind check runs per bundle over the cases that survived the missing-file check.

**`files` (`arms.ts`, `cases.ts`).**

- S1 (should-fix) — `caseFileProblem` accepts an entry whose first segment below `evals/files/` is `.claude`, and `placeCaseFiles` copies it into both arms' projects. No case uses `files` on this head, so no turn is affected today; the hole is in the accept-set this PR introduces. Three reachable effects, each from one committed catalog entry:
  - `evals/files/.claude/skills/BUNDLE/rules/x.md` (no `SKILL.md`) puts part of the bundle under test into the no-skill arm. The init line lists nothing, so `verdictOf` does not read the turn as `invalid`, and the no-skill answer is graded as if it had no skill.
  - `evals/files/.claude/skills/OTHER/SKILL.md` puts a whole skill under a non-catalog name into the no-skill arm. `bundlesLoaded` is the init line filtered to catalog bundles (`run.ts`, `judgeTurn`), so it is not seen either.
  - `evals/files/.claude/skills/BUNDLE/SKILL.md` overwrites the bundle under test on the with-skill arm (`cpSync` replaces by default), and `evals/files/.claude/settings.json` is read by both arms under `--setting-sources project`, hooks included.
  
  This contradicts the dry-run line (`no-skill no skill`) and the arm contract in `arms.ts` (the arms differ in exactly one thing, whether the bundle sits in `.claude/skills/BUNDLE/`). The fix is one condition in `caseFileProblem` refusing `.claude` as the first segment below `evals/files/`, with a row in the reader's refusal test. `.mcp.json` is inert under `--strict-mcp-config` and needs no refusal.

**The 11 assertion edits.** Each was read against the case's prompt, its `expected_output` and the bundle's text on `main`.

- `objectstack-automation/flows-triggers-approvals#13`, `hotcrm.custom` to `.custom`: holds. The skill says "the base's paired `.custom` package"; `overrides:`, `basedOn` and `/toggle` still carry the case.
- `objectstack-data/hooks-security-seeds-datasources#14`, forbid `****` to `'138****`: holds. The prompt and `references/seeds.md` both carry `138****4207`, so a right answer quotes it. A masked value under another prefix escapes the token, but the same wrong answer is still caught by `'N/A'` or by the required `@example.com`.
- `objectstack-data/objects-fields-relationships#10`, forbid `required: true` to `required: true,` and `required: true }`: holds. Both common authored forms are caught; the expected answer declines `required` by name.
- `objectstack-data/objects-fields-relationships#12`, `filter: { status: 'completed' }` to `filter:`: holds. The prompt names neither the field nor the value.
- `objectstack-data/objects-fields-relationships#14`, `value: 'active'` to `value: '`: holds. The forbidden `value: '合作中'` carries the point and is not bound to formatting.
- `objectstack-ui/views-apps-actions-pages#16`: holds. The URL template stays exact; `seed:` and `path: 'token'` release only the formatting and the author's param name.
- `objectstack-ai/skills-tools-knowledge#5`, forbid `defineAgent(` to `defineAgent({`: holds. An authored call is caught on one line or many.
- `objectstack-ai/skills-tools-knowledge#6`, `pendingActions.list` dropped: holds. The skill names the list door as `GET /api/v1/ai/pending-actions`; the refusal tokens carry the case.
- `objectui/testing#2`, `React Testing Library` to `@testing-library/react`: holds. `guides/testing.md` imports it in every example.
- `objectstack-upgrade/protocol-major-upgrade#3`, `never executed` dropped and the forbid narrowed: holds. The skill says "never ran" and "unexecuted", and the prompt carries the old forbidden token verbatim.
- `objectstack-i18n/bundles-locales-coverage#10`, forbid `verdict: {` to `verdict: { summary: '`: holds for the card's purpose (a right answer that quotes the wrong shape now passes), with N1 below.

**The 30 context sentences.** Each adds only that the project is not on disk and what the answer should carry. The two that add facts check out against `main`: `objectstack-api/endpoints-auth-routes#2` restates what case #1's expected output defines (path, `type: 'object_operation'`, `acme_lead`, 30 seconds), and `#6` gives the body in the shape `export.zod.ts` documents for `POST /api/v1/data/:object/import`. None of the added text contains a required token of its own case.

**The 42 trigger cases.** Seven per bundle, five positive and two negative, each file in the shape the reader accepts (`id`, `prompt`, `should_trigger`, `files: []`). Every neighbour negative matches a "Do not use" clause in the bundle's description on `main` (query #7 against "a list view's filter rules", ui #6 against flows that branch, automation #6 against the object layer), except formula #6 (N3).

No must-fix. One should-fix: S1.

Nits:

- N1 (nit): in `bundles-locales-coverage#10` the narrowed forbid is the only token that separates the nested shape from the right one, and it matches that shape on one line only. A wrong answer written across lines that also echoes `verdict.summary` from the prompt passes. Requiring the authored key `'verdict.summary'` (quoted, as a dotted key must be) would carry the point without binding the layout. The same one-line limit applies to `protocol-major-upgrade#3` and `objects-fields-relationships#12`, where other tokens still carry the case.
- N2 (nit): a `Grep` in content mode over `.claude/skills/BUNDLE/` reaches the skill's text and is not load evidence. The record keeps tool names but not the Grep path, so a later rule could not regrade an old round for it. The rule is the same before and after #34769, so that comparison holds.
- N3 (nit): `objectstack-formula/triggers#6` (an ObjectQL filter) has no "Do not use" clause behind it in the formula description on `main`, so a load there is not clearly wrong today. It becomes a fair case once #34769 adds one.
- N4 (nit): the per-bundle trigger table merges Skill-tool loads and read-only loads into one rate; only the per-case table splits them. A read-only load does not depend on the description, so the eval seat should compare #34769 on the Skill-tool column.
- N5 (nit): the PR body says each bundle's two negatives are one neighbour and one outside near miss. In the tree, query has two neighbours and i18n has two outside near misses.

This reviews the delta from L1 6963961238 (ACCEPT at `8d82dcb9`). The delta is one commit, `c169dc85` (4 files, +32 / -3), with no main merge. It answers the seat's S1, which is my N3. Dev report 6965169567.
